P1.evidence: No setter suffix on the title, no setter named, and no application referenced, so the read-back check does not apply. The standard two-part frame ran — 'where are you today? Where do you want to be? If we can help, I can go with one of the many options that we have' — missing 'what's in the way' and 'what you need'. Open question ran verbatim: 'So I'll leave the floor to yourself, Grant. How can we potentially help you?'

P2.evidence: Phase 2 did not happen. Not one of the nine checks was asked. Age (33), current weight (208 lb), target (190), occupation (financial advisor) and current gym work all arrived because the prospect volunteered them inside answers to other questions. Height, health conditions, injuries, diet, sleep and energy were never established at all. The most costly omission is P2d: the prospect volunteered back problems from old sports injuries and pain on everyday movement, and the rep did not ask a single follow-up before closing him on a kettlebell programme.

P3.evidence: Efficient and genuinely good. Refused the vague opening and pinned it down — 'when you say get back to yourself, which version of Grant are you referencing?' — producing 190 lb and the body-fat target. The 1-10 athletic potential scale then surfaced conditioning as the real weak point. Bridged out cleanly with 'Are there any other areas in your life where you notice you showing up as a 5 or 6 out of 10?' and 'what are the other arenas that you're hoping being a higher standard physically is going to have a positive ripple effect into?', which produced Cooper, the wife, and client-facing intensity at work. Only 'something you want to do but can't' never ran, which is where the back issue would have surfaced properly.

P4.evidence: The root-cause question ran well — 'what do you feel like is the main reason why we're not at our 10 out of 10 self?' — and the prospect named the gap himself: restart spurts, no plan, doing too much at once, burning out. Past attempts were only touched in passing and never asked for directly. P4f is a clear miss and a notable one on this call specifically: the prospect had just said 'I've actually followed his content for a while and used a lot of his workouts on my own', which is the exact opening for 'the information isn't the problem, so why can't you stick to it on your own?' and it was never taken.

P5.evidence: Skipped rather than run, and the rep said why out loud: 'Thanks for making my life easy, Grant. You know, some people you really have to kind of challenge politely on these conversations, but you seem to have a lot of self-awareness.' P5a was gestured at through a leading question — 'Is it just upon reflection of where you used to be, or is it perhaps a fear of where the trajectory could be for yourself?' — which supplied the answer rather than eliciting it. The want-or-need question stood in for the settle check and got 'I would say it's definitely both.' No 'why not', no line in the sand. An easy prospect got the least consequence work.

P6.evidence: The 1-10 trust check ran and returned a strong answer — 'I definitely think I need it. Like I said, I need that structure... I feel like it's a good system, good structure, and I want to jump in with it' — followed by the useful counterfactual 'if you had this when you're 30, where would you be today at 33?' But P6a's actual question about believing he can get there with the right structure never ran, and neither did the internally-capable question this rep uses on most other calls. P6b missed again. P6c is a hit only because a clear yes happened to arrive unprompted.

P11.evidence: Only observable to the threshold. The rep began the onboarding walkthrough and then removed the Fathom notetaker to take personal information, so no payment is witnessed. The Trevor call was described as a process step but no slot was offered or booked on the record, and there is no mention anywhere in this transcript of an agreement email, a signature, a welcome email, a Skool link or an onboarding questionnaire. Scored on evidence, with the caveat that steps may have occurred after recording stopped.

objection_plays.detail: No money objection and no hesitation of any kind. The prospect raised payment himself before the number was given — 'how does all this work as far as, you know, how are you paying for this?' — heard $6,000 and $9,000, and selected a tier without comment on cost.

The clinical gap again, in its quietest and therefore most easily missed form. The prospect raised, in substance, an ongoing back problem with pain on movement: 'from old sports injuries, you know, I feel like I have bad back issues, know, just moving around. And that's my big thing.' There is no scripted gate that obliges the rep to stop and qualify a spinal complaint, so nothing happened — no question about what the injury is, how long it has been there, whether anyone has assessed it, or whether loaded ballistic work is appropriate. The response was the standard designed-to-be-fluid line and the call closed four minutes later. A process defect, not a rep failure.

notes: An 18-minute call that closed at full price with zero resistance, and the brevity is the finding. Phase 3 was genuinely well run and Phase 4 got the gap named. But Phase 2 was skipped entirely and Phase 5 was skipped deliberately because the prospect was agreeable — the rep said as much on the record. The cost lands in one place: a disclosed back injury with everyday pain passed through the call without a single question and the man was sold a loaded kettlebell programme. Coach the health questions as non-optional regardless of how easy the call feels, and coach P4f here specifically, since the prospect was already using the free workouts and nobody asked why that was not enough.
